title: Opposite quasicategories reverse mapping spaces and composition
statement: Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces, arrow mapping spaces, and simplicial functors as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a simplicial set $X$, define $X^{\mathrm{op}}$ by $(X^{\mathrm{op}})_n=X_n$ and $\alpha^*_{X^{\mathrm{op}}}=(\alpha^\vee)^*_X$, where $\alpha^\vee(i)=n-\alpha(m-i)$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$. For every quasicategory $\mathcal C$ and vertices $x,y$, there is a natural equivalence of spaces, represented by a zigzag of weak homotopy equivalences using the natural right-pinch maps of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(y,x)$. These equivalences are natural under simplicial functors and carry the canonical composition and identity classes of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] to the reversed composition and identity classes. Thus precomposition and postcomposition maps are carried to the corresponding reversed maps. The comparisons also identify the coherent triangle witnesses for composition, including their images under simplicial functors. In particular they compare the specified commutation homotopies in the precomposition and postcomposition squares induced by a functor.

source.place: Kerodon Notation 1.4.2.1, Construction 1.4.2.2 and Remarks 1.4.2.3–1.4.2.6 (003L), together with the right-pinch comparison, Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5). The natural composition-compatible zigzag is agent-formulated from simplex reversal and the cited pinch/composition constructions. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags; no Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Write $\vartheta_n:\Delta^n\to(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}$ for the map which sends an $m$-simplex $\gamma:[m]\to[n]$ to $\gamma^\vee$. The identities $(\beta\alpha)^\vee=\beta^\vee\alpha^\vee$ and $(\alpha^\vee)^\vee=\alpha$ show that opposite is a functor, is involutive, and commutes with degreewise products. The map $\vartheta_n$ is an isomorphism and sends face $i$ to face $n-i$. Consequently a horn $\Lambda_i^n\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ reverses to $\Lambda_{n-i}^n\to\mathcal C$. For $0<i<n$ the latter is inner and has a filler, whose reversal fills the original horn. Thus $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasicategory. The same calculation with all horn indices proves that opposite preserves Kan complexes. These conclusions use precisely the horn definitions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Notation 1.4.2.1, Construction 1.4.2.2, Proposition 1.4.2.6 and Variant 1.4.2.8; explicit operator calculation

proof.text:
Use the fixed-vertex simplicial sets $H$ defined in [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. For every $k\geq1$ and list $x_0,\ldots,x_k$, define
$$R_k:H_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(x_0,\ldots,x_k)\longrightarrow H_{\mathcal C}(x_k,\ldots,x_0)^{\mathrm{op}}$$
by sending $\sigma:\Delta^k\times\Delta^m\to\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$ in degree $m$ to $\sigma^{\mathrm{op}}(\vartheta_k\times\vartheta_m)$. For $\alpha:[l]\to[m]$, the identity $\vartheta_m\Delta(\alpha)=(\Delta(\alpha^\vee))^{\mathrm{op}}\vartheta_l$ verifies the simplicial operators, including degeneracies. Repeating reversal gives its inverse. A restriction along $\beta:[j]\to[k]$ becomes restriction along $\beta^\vee$, by the same identity in the first factor. Postcomposition with any functor $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ commutes strictly with these formulas. In particular $R_1$ identifies $U_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)$ with $U_{\mathcal C}(y,x)^{\mathrm{op}}$. The opposite on this last mapping simplicial set is essential.

source.place: Construction 1.4.2.2 applied to the multiarrow fibers of Kerodon 01PF, Notation 4.6.8.1; explicit calculation

proof.text:
For any simplicial set $K$, define
$$r_K:|K^{\mathrm{op}}|\longrightarrow|K|,\qquad [a,(t_0,\ldots,t_m)]\longmapsto[a,(t_m,\ldots,t_0)].$$
If $b_m$ denotes coordinate reflection on the topological simplex, then $b_m|\alpha|=|\alpha^\vee|b_l$ for $\alpha:[l]\to[m]$: the coefficient at $j$ on both sides is $\sum_{\alpha(i)=m-j}t_i$ (on the right, substitute $i=l-h$ in the sum indexed by $\alpha^\vee(h)=j$). Hence the formula respects the realization quotient of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. It is continuous on each characteristic simplex, so continuous on the quotient; its inverse is the same formula for $K^{\mathrm{op}}$. Naturality follows by applying a simplicial map to $a$. Under the finite-product homeomorphism of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], $r_{K\times L}$ is $r_K\times r_L$: composing with each projection proves the assertion. Thus reflection respects all maps, products, and restriction diagrams used below.

source.place: Example 1.4.2.5; barycentric reflection and its quotient/product calculation

proof.text:
Use $\operatorname{Sing}$ and the unit $u_K$ of [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak]. The natural zigzag
$$K^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{u_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}}\operatorname{Sing}|K^{\mathrm{op}}|\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Sing}(r_K)}\operatorname{Sing}|K|\xleftarrow{u_K}K$$
consists of weak homotopy equivalences: both units are such by that node, with no Kan or nonemptiness requirement; the middle map is a simplicial isomorphism because $r_K$ is a homeomorphism. The two singular complexes are Kan. Indeed, the realization--singular adjunction and realized horn-pair homeomorphism of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identify a singular horn with a continuous map from $D^{m-1}\times\{0\}$; precompose it with the projection $D^{m-1}\times[0,1]\to D^{m-1}\times\{0\}$ to extend over the whole simplex. This applies for $m\geq1$, including both outer horns for $m=1$. The unit is natural since $|f|[a,t]=[f(a),t]$.

source.place: Theorem 3.6.4.1, and Example 1.4.2.5 (003L); singular horn fillers written using the cited realized-pair theorem

proof.text:
For either quasicategory $\mathcal B=\mathcal C$ or $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$, [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] supplies Kan complexes $M_{\mathcal B}(a,b)$, $U_{\mathcal B}(a,b)$ and the actual natural homotopy equivalence $j_{\mathcal B,a,b}$. This map is also a weak homotopy equivalence in the stated realization convention: realize its inverse and its two simplicial cylinder homotopies, using [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] for the ordinary-product cylinders, then apply [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. Consequently, putting $K=U_{\mathcal C}(y,x)$, the required zigzag is
$$M_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)\xrightarrow{j}U_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(x,y)\xrightarrow{R_1}K^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{u}\operatorname{Sing}|K^{\mathrm{op}}|\xrightarrow{\operatorname{Sing}(r_K)}\operatorname{Sing}|K|\xleftarrow{u}K\xleftarrow{j}M_{\mathcal C}(y,x).$$
All its objects are Kan, by steps 1 and 4 and the pinch node, and all arrows are weak homotopy equivalences. Every arrow commutes with the maps induced by $G$, by step 2, step 3, the unit formula, and the naturality assertion of the pinch node. No natural choice of an inverse is required.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10; natural right-pinch maps followed by the explicit reflection/unit zigzag

proof.text:
For clarity this zigzag represents, on realizations, exactly the reflection comparison of step 3. Define $\varepsilon_T:|\operatorname{Sing}T|\to T$ by $[s,t]\mapsto s(t)$. It respects the quotient relations, is continuous there, is natural in $T$, and satisfies $\varepsilon_{|A|}|u_A|=1_{|A|}$. For Kan $A$, the unit $u_A$ has a simplicial homotopy inverse by [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse], since step 4 proves that its source and target are Kan and that it is weak. Realizing its inverse homotopies by [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder] shows that $|u_A|$ is invertible in continuous homotopy classes. Thus $[\varepsilon_{|A|}]=[|u_A|]^{-1}$. Naturality of $\varepsilon$ gives
$$[\varepsilon_{|K|}]\,[|\operatorname{Sing}(r_K)|]\,[|u_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}|]=[r_K].$$
So the middle three arrows of step 5 realize to $[r_K]$, with the stated orientations. Write $\bar R_k=r_H|R_k|$ for the corresponding homeomorphism on realized $H$ spaces. Products of these comparisons are the comparisons of products by step 3. This identifies the zigzag used, rather than merely asserting existence of some equivalence. The same Whitehead node makes every arrow of step 5 invertible in simplicial homotopy classes, since its Kan and weak-equivalence hypotheses were all checked there.

source.place: Unit formula of Theorem 3.6.4.1 and the Kan Whitehead theorem (00UB); evaluation calculation

proof.text:
Write $\theta,\ell$ for the consecutive-edge and long-edge maps of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and use primes for $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}$. On the reversed triple $(d,b,a)$, step 2 gives the exact identities after realization
$$|\theta_{d,b,a}|\bar R_2=\tau(\bar R_1\times\bar R_1)|\theta'_{a,b,d}|,\qquad |\ell_{d,b,a}|\bar R_2=\bar R_1|\ell'_{a,b,d}|,$$
where $\tau$ exchanges the two inputs. Explicitly the old edges $12,01,02$ become $01,12,02$, respectively; hence the swap, including when vertices coincide. By the composition node both $\theta$ maps are homotopy equivalences and arrow composition has class $[\ell][\theta]^{-1}$. Multiplying the first equality by these inverses and using the second gives
$$\bar R_1\,C'_{a,b,d}=C_{d,b,a}\,\tau(\bar R_1\times\bar R_1)$$
in homotopy classes. Here and below realization of the homotopies uses [lem-coef-simplicial-realization-cylinder]. If $J=[j]$, the same node characterizes right-pinched composition by $Jc=C(J\times J)$. Conjugating this equation by the zigzag of step 5 (whose arrow part is $\bar R_1$ by step 6) proves that it carries $c'$ to $c$ with the inputs exchanged. This is an equality of space morphism classes, not merely a statement about their components. Finally [lem-cbc-kan-realization-mapping-classes] detects equality of these classes on realizations: its bijection applies with source the product of the two Kan mapping spaces and target the Kan output mapping space. Choose homotopy inverses to the zigzag arrows as in step 6; naturality of that bijection identifies their realized classes with the inverses used above. Its injectivity gives exactly the asserted equality in simplicial homotopy classes, independent of those choices.

source.place: Construction 4.6.8.9; reversal of the three edge restrictions and cancellation in the defining composition equation

proof.text: The identity vertex is a degenerate edge. Its reversal is the same degenerate edge at the same vertex, $j$ fixes that vertex by its explicit pinch formula, and $r_K$ fixes every realized vertex. The unit $u$ sends a vertex to its constant singular simplex, so the identity class also survives every arrow of the zigzag. Now fix an edge in either input of the composition equation in step 7. By [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], these restrictions are exactly precomposition and postcomposition. Since reversal swaps the two inputs and reverses the endpoints of the fixed edge, precomposition becomes postcomposition by the reversed edge and postcomposition becomes precomposition. This argument covers identities and repeated objects without a nonidentity assumption.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.8.11 and Notation 4.6.8.15; identity and fixed-input restriction calculation

proof.text:
Retain witnesses, rather than only the equation of classes. A triangle witness is a simplex $\sigma$ in $H_{\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,b,d)$, with its three edge restrictions. For every degree $m$, $R_2(\sigma)=\sigma^{\mathrm{op}}(\vartheta_2\times\vartheta_m)$ reverses its vertices and the three edge restrictions exactly as in step 7. The same formula for $R_k$ retains higher simplices and the face and degeneracy witnesses of [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine]. On realization its value on a parameterized simplex is
$$\bar R_k[\sigma,t]=[R_k(\sigma),b_m(t)].$$
For $m=1$, this says to reverse the parameter inside the reversed simplex, so the endpoints of the resulting path are precisely the images of the original endpoints. Thus it compares the homotopy itself. For a functor $G$, one has $(G^{\mathrm{op}}\sigma)^{\mathrm{op}}(\vartheta_k\times\vartheta_m)=G\bigl(\sigma^{\mathrm{op}}(\vartheta_k\times\vartheta_m)\bigr)$. Hence the witness and its image under $G$ are compared by the same formula. In particular, if $s$ is a chosen triangle-family representing composition before applying $G$, and $s'$ is such a family in the target, a specified homotopy between $G s$ and $s'(G\times G)$ is carried to its reversed triangle-family homotopy. Applying long-edge restriction gives the comparison of commutation homotopies for composition; fixing either input gives the asserted precomposition and postcomposition squares. The natural pinch maps and natural unit zigzags commute with these restrictions. This concerns the transported specified witness, and does not identify two independently chosen homotopies.

source.place: Notation 4.6.8.1, Remark 4.6.8.7 and Construction 4.6.8.9; explicit parameterized triangle and functor calculation
